verdict.rationale: Mollie documents a broad first-party API surface covering payments, refunds, subscriptions, payment links, chargebacks, balances, settlements, webhooks and Connect split payments, and refunds are explicitly available both by API and in the Web app. However, no evidence claims or demonstrates full parity between the dashboard UI and the API, and some areas such as chargebacks are documented only as retrieval. missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, evidence of API coverage for dashboard-only functions (account/profile settings, onboarding, settlement report generation), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Payments API is at the heart of the Mollie API. It allows you to create and manage payments.
Next to the API endpoint, you can also create refunds manually via the Mollie Web app.
The Subscriptions API provides an easy way to schedule recurring payments at regular intervals.
The Balances API allows you to retrieve real-time as well as historical information about your Mollie balance.
The Chargebacks API then allows you to retrieve details of the chargebacks that took place on your account.

Currently, the following APIs are available: Balances API, Captures API, Customers API, Invoices API, Mandates API, Methods API, Payments API, Payment Links API, Settlements API, Subscriptions API, Terminals API, Webhooks API, Webhook Events API.
